edges.description: Loss of adaptive reserve across secretory and metabolic tissues contributes to the multisystem growth failure; the intervening steps are not resolved.
Renal involvement is attributed to the same loss of stress-buffering capacity, but the tissue-specific mechanism is uncharacterized.
Central nervous system involvement is ascribed to the same loss of adaptive capacity, with the intervening steps unresolved.
Insufficient hematopoiesis is attributed to the same mechanism, though its tissue-specific basis is not worked out.
Thyroid dysfunction is ascribed to the same loss of stress-buffering reserve, with uncharacterized intermediates.
Exocrine pancreatic failure reflects the same loss of adaptive capacity in a high-secretory tissue; the intervening steps are not resolved.
Loss of beta-cell mass and function removes the source of endogenous insulin.
Insufficient endogenous insulin produces permanent insulin-dependent diabetes.
Repeated stress-triggered hepatocyte injury manifests clinically as recurrent acute hepatic failure.
Hepatocyte dysfunction impairs hepatic glucose production.
Loss of hepatic glucose output predisposes to recurrent hypoglycemia.
Impaired epiphyseal ossification produces the multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.

nodes.description: PERK is specifically required during the fetal and early-neonatal window for beta-cell proliferation, differentiation, and proinsulin trafficking. PERK-null beta cells fail to expand, show low beta-cell mass and distended endoplasmic reticulum with retained proinsulin, and undergo apoptosis. In patients the pancreas is hypoplastic with small islets and markedly reduced beta cells. The developmental requirement is what makes the resulting diabetes permanent and very early in onset.

nodes.description: PERK normally phosphorylates eIF2-alpha at Ser51, attenuating cap-dependent translation and engaging the PERK arm of the unfolded protein response. Without functional PERK this translational brake is lost, so the cell cannot slow protein synthesis when misfolded protein accumulates in the endoplasmic reticulum. The parallel IRE1 and ATF6 arms cannot fully compensate.

nodes.description: At baseline hepatocytes tolerate PERK deficiency, but intercurrent illness or metabolic stress raises the folding and synthetic load past the reduced reserve, triggering acute hepatocyte injury. This is why hepatic disease presents as intermittent, virally triggered non-autoimmune hepatitis that can progress to acute hepatic failure, rather than as constant liver disease.

nodes.description: Without the PERK-branch response, misfolded and unfolded protein accumulates in the endoplasmic reticulum of cells with high secretory or synthetic demand. This chronic, unbuffered endoplasmic reticulum stress is the shared cellular insult that branches to the pancreatic, hepatic, and skeletal phenotypes; it is a loss of adaptive reserve rather than a constant baseline organ failure, which is why hepatic injury in particular is episodic and stress-triggered.
